scope: cloud task HTTP lifecycle, queue recovery and lock boundaries
source_changes: POST /cloud/tasks validates transport configuration and durably inserts a task under a short submit lock independent from the long-lived execution queue lock, then returns task_id before remote work.
CloudTaskQueue::submit_persisted shares command/workspace validation and allocates the next persisted ID without loading or rewriting another active task record.
CLI cloud submit --run now executes its submitted task ID through the same retry-to-terminal path as the HTTP runner instead of one attempt on the first queued item.
GET status and result read a validated task JSON snapshot without waiting for the CloudTaskQueue execution lock.
Active cancellation uses watch::Sender::send_replace and returns cancel_requested; the runner owns remote cancellation, terminal persistence and SSE completion.
CloudTaskQueue checks a pre-existing cancellation signal before entering Running or starting remote submission.
HTTP queue initialization recovers persisted records, writes recovered Running tasks back as Queued and rejects unsafe or mismatched task identities.

Recovered and newly submitted queued tasks receive dispatch tokens; the runner snapshots token-backed queued IDs, executes each ID specifically and consumes its token so concurrent runner wakeups do not immediately rerun a retry.
Server OpenAPI and TypeScript OpenAPI/type descriptions reflect asynchronous submit and cancellation-request semantics.

Retryable remote failures now stay in one cancellable run_task_to_terminal_with_cancel lifecycle with backoff until a terminal state; the server consumes the dispatch token only after that lifecycle ends.
